title: Psalms Chapter 68 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 68 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 68 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 68.

questions.question: In Psalms 68, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: This phrase appears in Psalms 68:1, which is the first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: What is compared to smoke being driven away in Psalms 68?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:2 states, 'as smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.'

questions.question: What should the righteous do according to Psalms 68?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:3 says, 'But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God: yea, let them exceedingly rejoice.'

questions.question: What name is associated with God in Psalms 68:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:4 mentions, 'extol him that rideth upon the heavens by his name JAH.'

questions.question: Who does God represent in Psalms 68:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:5 states, 'A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.'

questions.question: What does God do for the solitary according to Psalms 68:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:6 says, 'God setteth the solitary in families.'

questions.question: What happened when God marched through the wilderness according to Psalms 68:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:8 states, 'The earth shook, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God.'

questions.question: What did God send according to Psalms 68:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:9 mentions, 'Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain.'

questions.question: What has God prepared for the poor in Psalms 68:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:10 states, 'thou, O God, hast prepared of thy goodness for the poor.'

questions.question: What did the Lord give according to Psalms 68:11?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:11 states, 'The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.'

questions.question: What did kings of armies do in Psalms 68:12?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:12 mentions, 'Kings of armies did flee apace.'

questions.question: God is the father of the fatherless according to Psalms 68.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:5 states, 'A father of the fatherless... is God.'

questions.question: The congregation dwells in the land prepared by God in Psalms 68.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:10 states, 'Thy congregation hath dwelt therein.'

questions.question: Psalms 68 states that God is only a judge of the rich.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:5 indicates God is a judge of the widows, not just the rich.

questions.question: Psalms 68 states that the heavens did not drop at the presence of God.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:8 states, 'the heavens also dropped at the presence of God.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 68 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 68 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will the wings of a dove be covered with according to Psalms 68:13?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:13 states, 'Though ye have lien among the pots, yet shall ye be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and her feathers with yellow gold.' This indicates that the wings of a dove will be adorned with silver and gold.

questions.question: What does Psalms 68:14 promise will happen when the Almighty scatters kings?
options: It will be white as snow in Salmon
questions.correctAnswer: It will be white as snow in Salmon
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:14 states, 'When the Almighty scattered kings in it, it was white as snow in Salmon,' suggesting that the scattering results in purity and brightness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 68:15, how is the hill of God described?
options: As a high hill like Bashan
questions.correctAnswer: As a high hill like Bashan
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:15 states, 'The hill of God is as the hill of Bashan; an high hill as the hill of Bashan,' indicating the greatness and significance of the hill of God.

questions.question: What is the significance of the hill mentioned in Psalms 68:16?
options: It is a place of worship
It is a site of battle
It is a place of sacrifice
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:16 states, 'Why leap ye, ye high hills? this is the hill which God desireth to dwell in,' emphasizing that this hill is chosen by God for His dwelling.

questions.question: According to Psalms 68:17, how many chariots of God are mentioned?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:17 states, 'The chariots of God are twenty thousand, even thousands of angels,' highlighting the vast number of God's chariots.

questions.question: What does Psalms 68:18 indicate about God’s actions?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:18 states, 'Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive,' indicating God's triumph over captivity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 68:19 say about God’s daily actions?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:19 states, 'Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits,' emphasizing God's continual blessings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 68:20 say God is the God of?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:20 states, 'He that is our God is the God of salvation,' affirming that God is the source of salvation.

questions.question: According to Psalms 68:21, what will God do to His enemies?
options: He shall wound the head of his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He shall wound the head of his enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:21 states, 'But God shall wound the head of his enemies,' indicating God's judgment upon His adversaries.

questions.question: What promise does God make in Psalms 68:22 regarding His people?
options: He will bring them again from Bashan
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring them again from Bashan
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:22 states, 'The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan,' which indicates God's intention to restore His people.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Psalms 68:23 regarding the enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:23 states, 'That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies,' using strong imagery to convey victory over adversaries.

questions.question: What do the goings of God signify in Psalms 68:24?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:24 states, 'They have seen thy goings, O God,' indicating that God's actions are visible and recognized.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 68:1 mentions the scattering of God's enemies.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:1 states, 'Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered,' affirming the scattering of God's enemies.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 68:6 describes God as the father of the fatherless.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:6 describes God as the father of the fatherless, but the statement is incorrect as the question asks for a different aspect.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 68:10 states that God has prepared for the poor.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:10 indeed states that God has prepared for the poor, but this statement is framed in a misleading context, thus marked as false.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 68 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 68.

questions.question: According to Psalms 68:25, who went before the procession?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:25 states, 'The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.' Therefore, the singers went before the procession.

questions.question: In Psalms 68:26, from where is the Lord blessed in the congregations?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:26 says, 'Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.' Thus, the Lord is blessed from the fountain of Israel.

questions.question: Which tribes are mentioned together with their rulers in Psalms 68:27?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:27 states, 'There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.' These tribes are mentioned together with their rulers.

questions.question: What does Psalms 68:28 request God to strengthen?
options: That which thou hast wrought for us
questions.correctAnswer: That which thou hast wrought for us
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:28 says, 'Thy God hath commanded thy strength: strengthen, O God, that which thou hast wrought for us.' The psalmist asks God to strengthen what He has done for them.

questions.question: According to Psalms 68:29, why shall kings bring presents?
options: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem
Because of thy mighty acts in battle
Because of thy covenant with Israel
Because of thy holy mountain Bashan
questions.correctAnswer: Because of thy temple at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:29 states, 'Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee.' The temple is the reason for the kings' gifts.

questions.question: In Psalms 68:30, what is God asked to do to the company of spearmen?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:30 says, 'Rebuke the company of spearmen, the multitude of the bulls... scatter thou the people that delight in war.' So God is asked to rebuke and scatter them.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'timbrel' (תְּפוּחִים) in Psalms 68:25 mean?
options: A type of hand drum or tambourine
A wind instrument like a trumpet
questions.correctAnswer: A type of hand drum or tambourine
questions.explanation: In Psalms 68:25, 'timbrels' refers to a percussion instrument, specifically a hand drum or tambourine, used in ancient Israelite worship.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 68:1-2 with the phrases 'Let God arise... let them also that hate him flee' and 'As smoke is driven away... as wax melteth before the fire'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:1-2 uses similes comparing the scattering of enemies to smoke driven away and wax melting before fire, explicitly employing similes.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God leading captivity captive as seen in Psalms 68:18?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 4:8 quotes Psalms 68:18 directly about God leading captivity captive, fulfilling the Old Testament theme of divine victory.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is connected to the shaking of the earth and heavens at God's presence as described in Psalms 68:8?
questions.explanation: Exodus 19:18 describes Mount Sinai shaking and smoke covering it when God descended, closely paralleling Psalms 68:8's imagery.

questions.question: What precedes Psalms 68:25 in the psalm's narrative?
options: A description of God bringing back His people
A call for kings to bring presents
A blessing of God in the congregations
An account of singing and rejoicing
questions.correctAnswer: An account of singing and rejoicing
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:24 states, 'They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary,' which introduces the theme of singing and rejoicing that continues in verse 25.

questions.question: What type of parallelism is found in Psalms 68:4: 'Sing unto God, sing praises to his name: extol him that rideth upon the heavens by his name JAH'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:4 repeats the idea of praising God with synonymous expressions, a hallmark of synonymous parallelism.

questions.question: Which typology is foreshadowed in Psalms 68:18 where it says 'thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive'?
options: Christ's ascension and victory over sin and death
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's ascension and victory over sin and death
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:18 is traditionally interpreted as a messianic foreshadowing of Christ's ascension and triumph over spiritual captivity, echoed in Ephesians 4:8.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 68:35 describes God as giving strength and power to His people from His holy places.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:35 states, 'O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power unto his people.' This confirms the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 68:31 says that only the princes of Israel will come out of Egypt to worship God.
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:31 says, 'Princes shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God.' It includes Ethiopia as worshippers, not only princes of Israel.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 68 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 68 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 68:5 teach about God's nature?
options: God as a father to the fatherless and judge of widows
God as a warrior who defeats His enemies
God as the creator of the heavens and the earth
God as the giver of earthly wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God as a father to the fatherless and judge of widows
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:5 states God is 'A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows,' emphasizing His compassionate and just nature toward the vulnerable.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s salvation is taught in Psalms 68:18?
options: God ascended on high, leading captivity captive and giving gifts to men, including the rebellious
God judges the nations and punishes the wicked
God creates all things visible and invisible
questions.correctAnswer: God ascended on high, leading captivity captive and giving gifts to men, including the rebellious
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:18 teaches that God’s salvation includes triumph over captivity and the giving of gifts even to rebels, showing a gracious and victorious salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s justice is found in Psalms 68:21?
options: God will wound the head of His enemies who persist in trespasses
God ignores the deeds of the wicked
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God will wound the head of His enemies who persist in trespasses
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:21 affirms God's active justice in punishing persistent sinners, showing His righteous judgment against sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 68:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:8 describes the earth shaking and Sinai moving at God's presence, illustrating His absolute sovereign power over creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Psalms 68:19?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:19 blesses the Lord who daily loads us with benefits, showing His faithful, ongoing provision and care.

questions.question: How does Psalms 68:7-10 connect to the broader biblical theme of God’s providential care for His people?
options: It portrays God leading His people through wilderness and providing for their inheritance
It shows God abandoning His people to their enemies
It emphasizes human effort over divine intervention
It teaches that God’s blessings are conditional on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays God leading His people through wilderness and providing for their inheritance
questions.explanation: Verses 7-10 recount God’s guidance through the wilderness and provision of rain to confirm the inheritance, reflecting biblical themes of covenantal care and providence.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Psalms 68:17-18 anticipate in the New Testament?
options: Christ’s ascension and His leading captivity captive
The exile of Israel into Babylon
The giving of the law at Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s ascension and His leading captivity captive
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:17-18 portrays God ascending on high and leading captivity captive, a theme later applied to Christ’s ascension and victory over sin and death (cf. Ephesians 4:8).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 68:5 and 68:6 teach about God's care for the marginalized?
options: God is both a protector of the fatherless and one who places the solitary into families
God ignores the plight of the poor
God punishes the weak without mercy
God’s care is limited to the righteous only
questions.correctAnswer: God is both a protector of the fatherless and one who places the solitary into families
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:5 calls God a father to the fatherless, and 68:6 says He sets the solitary in families, together teaching His protective provision for the vulnerable.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 68:19 and 68:20 teach about God’s salvation?
options: God daily provides benefits and is the God of salvation who controls death’s outcomes
God’s salvation is only for the righteous elite
Salvation depends on human works rather than God’s grace
Death ultimately prevails over God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: God daily provides benefits and is the God of salvation who controls death’s outcomes
questions.explanation: Verses 19 and 20 emphasize God’s continual blessings and His sovereign authority over death, affirming the doctrine of salvation by God’s power.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 68:31 and 68:32 teach about the universal scope of God's reign?
options: Kings and kingdoms from Egypt and Ethiopia to all the earth are called to worship God
God’s reign is limited only to Israel
Foreign nations are excluded from worship of God
God’s kingdom is purely spiritual and not related to earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: Kings and kingdoms from Egypt and Ethiopia to all the earth are called to worship God
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:31-32 invite nations and kingdoms far beyond Israel to worship God, showing the universal scope of His reign and sovereignty.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Psalms 68:1-3 encourages violence against God’s enemies and hatred. What does the text actually teach?
options: God’s enemies are scattered, but the righteous are called to rejoice before Him
God commands indiscriminate hatred and violence against all people
The text condones revenge without justice
The psalm promotes human-initiated violence without divine authority
questions.correctAnswer: God’s enemies are scattered, but the righteous are called to rejoice before Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:1-3 calls for God to arise and scatter His enemies, but emphasizes rejoicing for the righteous, showing divine justice rather than human hatred.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 68:15 teach regarding God’s dwelling place?
options: God’s dwelling is on a high and exalted hill, symbolizing His majesty
God dwells only in the hearts of individuals
God’s presence is limited to the temple’s interior only
God’s dwelling is indistinguishable from any earthly place
questions.correctAnswer: God’s dwelling is on a high and exalted hill, symbolizing His majesty
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:15 describes the hill of God as a high hill like Bashan, indicating the exalted, majestic nature of God’s dwelling.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is specifically demonstrated in Psalms 68:34?
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:34 states 'his excellency is over Israel,' highlighting the attribute of God's supreme excellence and glory.

questions.question: How does Psalms 68:24-27 function within the narrative arc of Israel’s worship tradition?
options: It describes organized worship with singers, instruments, and tribal leaders, emphasizing communal praise
It emphasizes individual prayer without community
It forbids music and singing in worship
It depicts only the king as responsible for worship
questions.correctAnswer: It describes organized worship with singers, instruments, and tribal leaders, emphasizing communal praise
questions.explanation: Verses 24-27 depict a structured worship procession including singers and tribal princes, reinforcing communal and ordered worship in Israel’s tradition.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 68:30 teach about God's judgment on those who delight in war?
options: God will scatter and rebuke the warriors until they submit
God blesses all who engage in war without restraint
God remains neutral in human conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: God will scatter and rebuke the warriors until they submit
questions.explanation: Psalms 68:30 calls for God to rebuke and scatter the multitude of warriors, showing His active judgment against those who delight in war.
